Lecture 9: Decline, an overview

No single event ended the League. This lecture weighs the causes historians give.

The League's trade fell by half over the sixty years before its last council.

Rival merchants from the southern port of Calver took over the amberwool trade.

Lecture 9: The plague claim

Older textbooks claim the League collapsed because of the Grey Fever plague.

The plague did kill many people in the coastal cities, which is why the claim is so easy to repeat.

This course does not accept it as the main cause; the next page explains why.

Lecture 9: Port Ashby silts up

Professor Quist argues the main cause of the decline was the silting of Port Ashby's harbour, which closed it to large ships.

Dredging records show Port Ashby's harbour depth fell from 8 metres to 3 metres.

Without its deep harbour the League lost the trade route that paid for its fleet.

Lecture 9: The last council

The last League council met in Dunmere.

At the last council only two cities sent delegates.

After it, the cities made separate treaties with Calver.
